requirements.behavior: Bare library and safe owned code
requirements.criterion: Default dependency tree has no process/transport/CLI/logging runtime; every target forbids unsafe; production panic audit is clean
Preserve native argv/env/cwd including non-ASCII and native non-Unicode values; typed spawn errors; no shell interpolation
Prepare endpoint/logs/scope before authorized execution; immediate output/exit retained; gated pre-Start EOF launches nothing

In captured pipe/terminal modes, workload survives foreground/detached client exit, crash, and terminal disconnect; monitor independent of caller session/job; passthrough documents its external I/O owner
Initial connection and later endpoint attach work; no replay race or unbounded historical backlog
One writer, bounded observers, release on disconnect, explicit pipe EOF; retained writer survives zero clients; Ctrl-D remains bytes
Force stop, leader exit, and timeout clean the supported workload tree; fork races, grandchildren, daemonization, and changed process groups are tested
Preserve leader native exit/signal/full Windows code and exit time; reap owned/adopted children; no fake success or stale-PID kill
Native PTY/ConPTY, controlling terminal/session, initial size, resize, interactive shell/job control, detach/reattach, drain/teardown
Safe adoption, exact inheritance, capture/pass/hold roles, no leaked writer copies, no argument rewriting or child-API proxy
Conmon-compatible timestamp/stream/F/P records; partial lines, binary pipe bytes, terminal merged output, extra source separation
File, journald where applicable, file+journal, none, passthrough; actual destination behavior and metadata match
Size/global cumulative caps, truncation, rotation/backup count, external reopen, tags/labels, partial metadata, path protection
Bounded queues/client count; sink backpressure and write failures explicit; stalled viewer isolated; control/deadline remains responsive
Default log synchronization and explicit opt-out; atomically retained result; sync/storage failures visible; crash claims precisely limited
Allowed sd_notify messages only, real service attribution, no invented readiness/heartbeat or arbitrary descriptor-store proxy
Correct inherited descriptors, LISTEN_FDS/LISTEN_FDNAMES semantics and actual child LISTEN_PID; unsupported host integration explicit
Monotonic deadline in monitor after native launch; works detached; kills workload scope and records timeout separately
Native membership established before child code/forks; monitor outside workload limits; external manager gate when needed
Linux cgroup v1/v2 events/final checks and evidence retention; SIGKILL never fabricated as OOM; other platforms report actual available evidence
Attempt permitted protection; failure visible; protection not inherited by workload or exit helper
Monitor-only reservations retained then released before final notification; endpoints cleaned; retained state remains readable
Native command/args/delay, no shell, no resource leaks; caller policy independent of original CLI; failure does not replace workload exit
Dillo cooperative cleanup via existing console loss, including full buffers; helpers accounted for; no immediate OS kill preempts cleanup
Fixed version, checked lengths/allocations, bounded malformed input; private native endpoint/ACL; separate diagnostics/log levels/native syslog where applicable; CLI help/version/API identity
Shared run/build launch, run/attach/logs/wait/stop, IDs/discovery/prune protection, terminal restore/detach/resize semantics
Original inherited named-port pipes, bidirectional v0 CBOR, guest-first ordering, virtiofs repo/cache/output remain unchanged
Missing results remain unknown; engine cleanup is idempotent; monitor death cannot claim a callback ran
Native Linux/macOS/Windows MSVC build and execution; reproducible locked dependencies, license inventory, package contains full binary and bare lib
Conmon-equivalent Unix signal forwarding without losing reaping/log finalization; native Windows cancellation semantics documented/tested; raw terminal bytes remain separate
